summary: John Muir studied at Glasgow, East India Company College, Fort William College, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1844, and later held a post at the University of Edinburgh.

John Murdoch worked in religious studies and Indology. Educated at the High School of Glasgow and the University of Glasgow (LL.D. 1878), he was Agent and Travelling Secretary in India for the Christian Vernacular Education Society (1858–1903) and a Madras University Fellow.

John Murray Mitchell was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, Marischal College, and the University of Edinburgh. He taught at Wilson College, Mumbai (1844–1866) and served as Principal of Duff College (1868–1873).

John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who founded the Bonpo Translation Project. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche (~1971–1987), Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (~1976), and Namkhai Norbu.

John N. Carpenter worked in religious studies and Indology. He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society, Principal of St. Paul's Divinity School (1900), at St. John's College, Agra, and as Principal of Emmanuel College (1916–1922).

John Nemec specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD 2005) under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher, he was appointed Associate Professor of Indian Religions and South Asian Studies at Virginia in 2004.

John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Richard Keith Sprigg, and Anna J. Allott. He worked as a research associate at SOAS University of London from 1959 to 1999.

John P. Keenan is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1980) under Minoru Kiyota, also studying under Noriaki Hakamaya. He was a Fellow at Nanzan University (1983–1986) and taught at Middlebury College.

John Peile was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge and under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen. At Cambridge, he served as Reader of Comparative Philology (1884–1893), Master of Christ's College (from 1887), and President of Newnham College (~1890–1909).

John Penry Lewis worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning a B.A. from Queen's University Belfast (~1872–1876), he served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1877 to 1910.

John Peter Jones was a religious studies and Indology scholar educated at Case Western Reserve and Andover Theological Seminary. He served as Principal of Pasumalai Seminary (1892–1914) and Professor of Indian Missions at Hartford Seminary from 1914.

John Peter Wade was a medical surgeon and scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh and was appointed Assistant Medical Surgeon for the East India Company in 1784.

John Pickford was an Indologist who studied at Brasenose College, University of Oxford (M.A. 1865) under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai (until 1872) and held a professorship at the University of Madras.

John Playfair, a scholar of Indology and other fields, studied at St Andrews and Edinburgh. He co-founded the Royal Society of Edinburgh (1783) and served as Professor of Mathematics at the University of Edinburgh (1785–1818).

John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who earned his doctorate from Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held chairs at the Australian National University (1995–2016) and Deakin University (2016–2022), later lecturing at Melbourne (2022).

John R. B. Campbell is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, also studying with the 14th Dalai Lama and other traditional teachers.

John R. McRae was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned his PhD from Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Cornell (~1983–1993), Indiana University Bloomington (~1993–2005), and Komazawa University (~2006–2008), and chaired the Numata Center.
John Riley Perks is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

John Ronald Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1987) under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, also studying at KCL and SOAS. He served on the faculty at Colgate University from ~1972 to 2013.
